subject: Recap & next steps — capacity pilot qualification for LuminaHealth
messages:
From: Alex Powell <alex.powell@luminahealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery call — capacity fit for inference

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick notes from Lumina's side to make sure we're aligned before you send a formal recap: 

- Pain: High latency variability (p95 spikes up to 800ms) during morning traffic bursts, causing failed UX handoffs. Also concerned about inference cost unpredictability across regions.
- Current stack: self-hosted Triton on k8s, mix of older T4s + a few rented A100s for peak jobs; using autoscaler but seeing slow cold-starts for new model versions.
- Data posture: PHI-adjacent workloads — need VPC isolation and proof of encryption at rest.
- Success criteria for pilot: demonstrate predictable sustained TPS during a 2-week simulated peak, maintain p95 < 200ms, and validate isolation controls.

Next asks from our side: pilot scope (what reserved pool size do you recommend), short plan for traffic shaping/traffic replay, and a rough quote for reserved capacity. Also loop in procurement once we have a pilot SOW.

— Alex
Alex Powell
Head of ML Platforms | LuminaHealth
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Powell <alex.powell@luminahealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T18:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call — capacity fit for inference (recap & pilot proposal)

Alex — thanks, great to meet. Recap below and proposed next steps. Quoting your original items for clarity: 

On Thu, Jun 10, 2026 at 3:22 PM Alex Powell <alex.powell@luminahealth.com> wrote:
> - Pain: High latency variability...
> - Current stack: self-hosted Triton on k8s...
> - Data posture: PHI-adjacent...
> - Success criteria for pilot: predictable sustained TPS, p95 < 200ms, validate isolation.

Our understanding (summary):
- Observable pain: bursty morning traffic causing cold-starts and queueing. You need both latency SLOs and cost predictability.
- Environment constraints: must run in a VPC or Private deployment topology; no model weights leave your control in the pilot.
- Primary goals for a successful pilot: (1) sustain a target baseline TPS with <200ms p95, (2) show autoscaling/burst behavior up to your peak, (3) verify isolation and KMS integration for keys.

How Redwood Dedicated maps to this: 
- Reserved GPU pools: assign a fixed pool (A100-equivalent) to guarantee baseline throughput and avoid noisy neighbors.
- Predictable TPS: we can size the pool to hit your baseline TPS; we use continuous batching and KV-cache warmup procedures to reduce p95.
- Autoscaling & burst: support for scheduled and demand-based burst to a shared burst pool; we can define a burst policy (max burst multiplier, cooldown windows, and failover to a smaller-but-faster model variant if capacity constrained).
- Isolation & security: Private control plane + customer VPC option, full KMS/HSM integration, audit logs exported to your SIEM.

Initial pilot proposal (scope & success metrics):
- Duration: 4 weeks (1 week prep/profiling, 2 weeks live traffic simulation, 1 week evaluation).
- Pilot footprint: reserved pool sized to match 2x your current A100 equivalent (we'll finalize after you send profile).
- Success criteria: sustained baseline TPS (your target), p95 < 200ms for 95% of test windows, verified KMS key rotation test, and a runbook for autoscale-to-burst behavior.

Requested items from LuminaHealth (deliverables required to size pilot):
1) Typical traffic shape (qps by minute/hour) and payload sizes (avg tokens).
2) A sanitized sample of representative prompts (for kernel/memory profiling).
3) Security questionnaire owner / contact for SOC2 evidence exchange.

Next steps & owners: 
- Action: Lumina to send traffic profile and sample prompts — owner: Alex — due: 2026-06-15
- Action: Redwood to send one-pager + mutual action plan template + pilot SOW draft — owner: tessa_morgan — due: 2026-06-12 (attached)
- Action: Schedule technical deep-dive to validate networking/VPC details — owner: vivek_kulkarni to propose slots — due: 2026-06-14

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_one-pager.pdf; mutual-action-plan-template.xlsx (attached). Also attaching a checklist for security evidence exchange.

Open items we'll cover in the technical deep-dive: placement of KV cache, expected cold-start time for new model variants, model quantization impacts on p95, and the exact burst policy parameters you prefer (max multiplier and cooldown).

If that aligns, we'll draft the SOW and sample pricing for a 4-week pilot. Thanks again — forwarding to Vivek and Evelyn for technical and security alignment.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Alex Powell <alex.powell@luminahealth.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call — capacity pilot qualification (technical questions)

Alex / team — a few technical clarifications to size the pilot correctly: 

1) Can you confirm average and 95th-percentile sequence lengths (tokens) for your top-5 flows? Even small increases in avg tokens materially change GPU memory pressure.
2) Do you have session affinity requirements or are requests stateless for routing? If you rely on long-lived KV caches per user, that affects pool sizing.
3) Are there any model variants you plan to test concurrently (e.g., full-precision + int8 fallback)? If yes, call that out.

Preliminary pilot sizing (estimate; we'll finalize after your profile): 
- Reserved baseline: equivalence of 2 x A100 GPU (dedicated pool) to cover sustained baseline TPS.
- Burst pool: shared burst capacity able to scale up to ~4x baseline for short windows (policy: 10-minute max, 30-minute cooldown).
- Monitoring: we will enable per-route token & latency breakdown and a heatmap for cold-starts.

I'll propose 3 slots for a deep-dive tomorrow morning. Also drafting a short SOW and a ballpark commitment figure to help procurement start internal approvals.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principle Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
